title: Learn Cloud Security
tagline: Secure cloud estates — identity, data, and infrastructure by design
description: A three-level curriculum for Cloud Security Engineers. Learn to harden AWS/Azure/GCP-style environments, automate guardrails, and respond to cloud incidents — always within authorized accounts and with least-privilege, privacy-aware practices.
prerequisites: Familiarity with one major cloud (AWS, Azure, or GCP) at a basic builder level
Comfort with IaC concepts (Terraform or CloudFormation/Bicep) or willingness to learn
Understanding that cloud actions can be irreversible — use sandbox accounts for practice

levels.title: Cloud Security Foundations
levels.goal: Harden accounts with strong identity, logging, and network baselines

topics.title: Authorized cloud work
items: Only use accounts and orgs you own or are granted access to
Sandbox vs. production: never experiment in prod
Data residency, privacy, and customer trust basics

topics.title: Shared responsibility model
items: What the provider secures vs. what you must secure
Common misconceptions ("the cloud is secure by default")
Mapping risks to identity, data, network, and workload layers

topics.title: IAM essentials
items: Users, roles, policies, and groups — least privilege
Avoiding long-lived access keys; preferring roles/federation
MFA, break-glass accounts, and password policies

topics.title: Resource policies
items: Bucket/blob and key policies that accidentally go public
Service principals / managed identities for apps
Reviewing who can assume powerful roles

topics.title: Visibility first
items: Turning on org/account audit trails and retaining them safely
Centralizing logs without exposing sensitive payloads
Alerts for root/admin use and policy changes

topics.title: Network & data basics
items: VPC/VNet segmentation and security groups / NSGs
Public vs. private endpoints
Encryption at rest/in transit and key ownership basics

projects: Document the shared responsibility model for your chosen cloud
Harden a sandbox account: MFA, logging, and block public storage defaults
Write least-privilege IAM roles for a simple app (read vs. deploy)
Create a baseline checklist for new cloud accounts in your org

levels.title: Guardrails, Workloads & Automation
levels.goal: Encode security as code and protect compute, data, and pipelines

topics.title: Preventive controls
items: Service control policies / org policies / Azure Policy concepts
OPA/Conftest or cloud-native policy for IaC reviews
CSPM findings: triage noise vs. real exposure

topics.title: Secure IaC
items: Terraform plan review for security regressions
Secrets in state and how to avoid them
Module standards for encryption, logging, and private networking

topics.title: Compute & containers
items: Hardening VMs/images and patch channels
Container image scanning and non-root runtimes
Kubernetes RBAC, network policies, and secrets (lab)

topics.title: Data protection
items: KMS/Key Vault patterns and separation of duties
Backup, immutability, and ransomware resilience
Classification and access reviews for sensitive datasets

topics.title: Pipeline security
items: OIDC federation from CI to cloud (no static keys)
Environment protection rules and approval gates
Artifact signing and provenance awareness

topics.title: Threat modeling cloud apps
items: Trust boundaries across accounts, VPCs, and SaaS
Metadata service and SSRF-to-cloud credential risks
Documenting abuse cases for new architectures

topics.title: Cloud-native detections
items: Suspicious IAM changes, data exfil patterns, and crypto mining signals
Wiring cloud findings into SIEM/SOC workflows
Authorized hunting queries against your own audit logs

projects: Add policy-as-code checks that block public storage and open admin ports
Secure a Terraform module set for a three-tier app (network, IAM, KMS)
Design OIDC-based deploy roles for CI with least privilege
Build a detection pack for five high-value cloud audit events

levels.title: Multi-Account Strategy & Incident Response
levels.goal: Design secure landing zones and lead cloud incident response

topics.title: Landing zones & org design
items: Account/subscription/project vending and isolation
Central security tooling vs. workload autonomy
Network hub-spoke / shared services security patterns

topics.title: Zero trust in cloud
items: Identity-first access to admin planes
Just-in-time elevation and session recording
Workload identity and service-to-service auth

topics.title: Cloud incident response
items: Containment: isolate principals, revoke keys, snapshot evidence
Forensics on ephemeral workloads and control-plane logs
Cross-account blast radius analysis

topics.title: Sophisticated attack patterns
items: Privilege escalation via mislinked roles and trust policies
Data exfiltration via storage and logging channels
Defensive validations with authorized red/purple team exercises

topics.title: Operating the program
items: Control frameworks mapped to cloud controls (CIS, NIST CSF)
Exception management and time-bounded risk acceptance
Metrics: exposure age, policy coverage, and IR readiness

topics.title: Multi-cloud & SaaS
items: Consistent identity and logging patterns across providers
SaaS security posture (SSO, SCIM, admin audit)
Vendor access and third-party risk in cloud estates

projects: Design a secure multi-account landing zone with guardrails and logging
Run a cloud IR tabletop (compromised deploy role) and publish a playbook
Produce a CIS/NIST control mapping for your primary cloud with gaps
Architect JIT admin access with monitoring and break-glass procedures
